title: Normality of fixed subrings and their prime localizations
statement: Let $D$ be a commutative integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $G$ be a group, and let $\alpha:G\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(D)$ be an action by unital ring automorphisms. Put $C=D^G=\{c\in D:\alpha_g(c)=c\text{ for every }g\in G\}$, with its inherited subring structure. Then $C$ is an integrally closed domain. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset C$, the localization $C_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is an integrally closed domain; consequently $C$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. No finiteness or faithfulness of the action, and no invertibility of a group order in $D$, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00GY, lemma-localize-normal-domain, including the common-denominator monic polynomial argument; the fixed-subring normality argument is agent-formulated for the existing quotients of ILO X 2.3 Step 2, p.151, and is retained from item proof step 6, followed by its step 7.

proof.text: Each $\alpha_g$ fixes $0,1$ and preserves sums, negatives and products, so $C$ is a unital subring of $D$. In particular $0\ne1$ in $C$ and a zero product in $C$ has a zero factor, since these facts hold in $D$. Thus $C$ is a domain. The rule $a/b\mapsto a/b$, for $a,b\in C$ and $b\ne0$, embeds $\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ into $\operatorname{Frac}(D)$: equality on either side is exactly $ab'=a'b$ in $D$, equivalently in $C$; the fraction addition and multiplication formulas agree.

source.place: Tags 0309 (definition-domain-normal), 00GV (definition-ring-normal), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); agent-written fixed-subring argument retained from the parent normal-quotient prerequisite.

proof.text: Let $x\in\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ satisfy a monic equation $x^n+\sum_{i<n}c_i x^i=0$, $c_i\in C$. Its image $y\in\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ satisfies the same equation with coefficients included in $D$. Integral closedness of $D$, in the stated definition of normal domain, gives $d\in D$ with $y=d$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(D)$.

source.place: Tags 0309 (definition-domain-normal), 00GV (definition-ring-normal), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); agent-written fixed-subring argument retained from the parent normal-quotient prerequisite.

proof.text: Write $x=a/b$ with $a,b\in C$, $b\ne0$. The equality $d=a/b$ implies $bd=a$ in $D$, by injectivity of $D\to\operatorname{Frac}(D)$. For any $g\in G$, applying $\alpha_g$ gives $b\alpha_g(d)=a=bd$, since $a,b$ are fixed. Cancellation of the nonzero $b$ in the domain $D$ yields $\alpha_g(d)=d$. Hence $d\in C$, and the embedding of step 1 gives $x=d$ already in $\operatorname{Frac}(C)$. Every such root is therefore in $C$, which is integrally closed by the normal-domain definition.

source.place: Tags 0309 (definition-domain-normal), 00GV (definition-ring-normal), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); agent-written fixed-subring argument retained from the parent normal-quotient prerequisite.

proof.text: For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset C$, put $S=C\setminus\mathfrak p$. Since $\mathfrak p$ is proper and prime, $1\in S$, $0\notin S$ and $S$ is multiplicatively closed. The prime-localization definition identifies $C_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}C$. Apply the localization-of-normal-domain lemma to the normal domain $C$ proved above and this $S$; it states that $S^{-1}C$ is a normal domain. Thus every $C_{\mathfrak p}$ is an integrally closed domain.

source.place: Tags 0309 (definition-domain-normal), 00GV (definition-ring-normal), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); agent-written fixed-subring argument retained from the parent normal-quotient prerequisite.

proof.text: The assertion that all prime localizations of $C$ are normal domains is precisely the definition of a normal ring. This proves the final conclusion. The only cancellation used a nonzero denominator in a domain; no step used finiteness or faithfulness of $G$, or division by its order.
